_comment: SHARED FIXTURE - one answer key for the queue subsystem, all four frameworks.
ADR-0024: the developer writes against the CONTRACT, never the PROVIDER.
Swapping file for rabbitmq, kafka or mongodb changes ONE env var and NOTHING
ELSE. Identical application code, identical OBSERVABLE outcome.
These are INVARIANTS, not a bug list. Eleven defects were measured in this
subsystem on 2026-08-01; each one is an instance of one of the six rules
below being broken. Stating the rules is what stops the twelfth.
Queues have the most open findings of any subsystem AND no fixture - which is
the whole correlation this file exists to break. Every subsystem that already
has a fixture (dispatch, health, dotenv, write-path) is one where drift stopped
HOW THIS IS CHECKED: scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py asserts that every
invariant naming a suite+cases has those cases present in all four frameworks.
An invariant with an empty 'cases' list is OWED - declared and not yet proven.
Owed is reported loudly and does not fail the build; a case that was named and
has since disappeared DOES fail, because that is a test someone deleted.

invariants.rule: Every public Queue method resolves and runs on EVERY configured backend. No method may be a fatal error, a NoMethodError, or a throw-at-construction on any backend the framework offers.
invariants.why: MEASURED: PHP failed()/deadLetters()/retryFailed() are a FATAL Error on rabbitmq and kafka; Ruby queue.size raises NoMethodError on kafka; Node rabbitmq and kafka THROW at construction, so an app that developed on file cannot start at all after the env var changes. The upgrade path is severed rather than degraded - the exact scenario ADR-0024 exists to protect.

invariants.rule: Every operation acts on the CONFIGURED backend. No method may silently read or write the local file store when another backend is selected.
invariants.why: MEASURED: PHP clear() and purge() always hit the local FILE store whatever backend is configured; Node popBatch() and popById() always read the local file store even on mongodb. The call appears to succeed and operates on the wrong data - a silent wrong answer, which is the worst failure class because nothing surfaces it.

invariants.rule: job.fail() reaches the backend on every provider, and a job past max_retries becomes observable through dead_letters() on every provider. A dead-letter handler written locally must find the same jobs after deploying onto a broker.
invariants.why: MEASURED: on Ruby rabbitmq/kafka the whole failure lifecycle silently no-ops - job.fail() never reaches the backend and dead_letters() is always empty. A developer tests retry-and-dead-letter locally on file, ships it, and the dead-letter queue is permanently empty in production with no error anywhere.

invariants.rule: delay_seconds / delay is honoured on every backend. A job pushed with a delay is not visible to a consumer before that delay elapses.
invariants.why: MEASURED: delay is silently DROPPED on every non-file backend, in ALL FOUR frameworks. A scheduled job fires immediately in production and on time in development. This one is unanimous across the family, which makes it a contract that was never written down rather than four independent bugs.
cases: an undelayed job is visible immediately
a delayed job is not visible before its delay elapses
a delayed job becomes visible once its delay elapses
a backend that cannot delay refuses instead of dropping the delay
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-03, against a live MongoDB, RabbitMQ and Kafka. The fix splits by what each broker can actually do. MONGODB: implemented - a delayed job is stamped available_at in the future, which every dequeue already filtered on. Each framework dropped it in its OWN place, which is why the symptom was unanimous but the patch is not: python's adapter never passed delay_seconds to enqueue; PHP's Queue::push built a SEPARATE message array for the external-backend branch carrying neither priority nor delay_seconds, so the value never reached the backend at all; ruby never WROTE available_at and never FILTERED on it, so writing it alone would have changed nothing; node wrote delayUntil but put five conditions in ONE $or, making the reservation gate and the delay gate alternatives instead of requirements - a fresh delayed job has no availableAt, matched {$exists: false}, and was handed straight to a consumer. RABBITMQ and KAFKA: they RAISE naming the backend and the operation (invariant 6), because neither has a per-message delay - rabbitmq's delayed-message-exchange is a non-core plugin and the TTL+dead-letter workaround head-of-line blocks, and kafka reads a partition in offset order. Node satisfies this half by refusing those backends outright at construction (ADR-0022). Every case is mutation-proved: reverting each framework's fix kills exactly 'a delayed job is not visible before its delay elapses' and nothing else.

invariants.rule: priority orders delivery, and a job that is not yet available is not delivered, on every backend that claims to support them.
invariants.why: MEASURED: Ruby + mongodb ignores priority and job availability entirely on the read path; Node + mongodb builds an availability predicate as an OR that always matches, so both delay and retryBackoff are inert. An always-true predicate is indistinguishable from a working one until timing matters.
cases: a higher priority job is delivered before an older lower priority one
equal priority jobs are delivered oldest first
a backend that cannot prioritise refuses instead of dropping the priority
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-03, against a live MongoDB, RabbitMQ and Kafka. The AVAILABILITY half was closed first by delay-is-honoured-on-every-backend (Ruby never filtered on available_at; Node's predicate was an always-true OR) and is not re-tested here. PRIORITY was honoured only on the file backend: MEASURED before the fix, mongodb ignored it in PHP, Ruby AND Node, and every broker ignored it in all four. Each framework lost it somewhere different. PHP built a SEPARATE message for the external-backend branch carrying no priority, and even once unified stored priority only INSIDE the message sub-document where a sort cannot reach, sorting on created_at alone. Ruby never WROTE the field its own dequeue read back (doc['priority'] || 0), and also sorted on created_at alone. Node's sort was RIGHT all along ({priority: -1, createdAt: 1}) but priority never ARRIVED - the QueueBackend interface had no such parameter and Queue.push passed it only to liteBackend, so the sort ordered on a field no document carried. Python was already correct and is the reference. MONGODB now stores priority top-level and sorts highest-first with ties oldest-first, matching the file backend's policy. RABBITMQ and KAFKA RAISE naming the backend and the operation (invariant 6): a RabbitMQ queue is FIFO and native priority needs the queue DECLARED with x-max-priority, which an existing queue cannot be redeclared with (PRECONDITION_FAILED), so enabling it would break every queue already in service; Kafka has no priority concept at all. Node satisfies that half by refusing both backends at construction (ADR-0022). Mutation-proved in all four: reverting each framework's fix kills exactly 'a higher priority job is delivered before an older lower priority one', and removing a refusal guard kills exactly the refusal case.

invariants.rule: A backend that genuinely cannot perform an operation RAISES, naming the backend and the operation. It may never silently no-op or return an empty result that is indistinguishable from success.
invariants.why: ADR-0024 rule 3: a method that exists and no-ops is worse than one that is absent, because absent fails loudly at the call site. Every silent-no-op finding in this subsystem would have been caught on the first run if this rule held.
cases: an unknown queue backend raises instead of silently using file
a queue backend name is normalised before it is resolved
the guard still accepts every documented backend name
invariants.status: PARTIALLY PROVEN in all four 2026-08-03: the BACKEND-SELECTION half. An unrecognised TINA4_QUEUE_BACKEND now RAISES naming the value and the valid set in all four (php + nodejs previously fell through to the local file store), and the name is normalised in all four (ruby previously normalised only the env var, so an explicit backend: 'FILE' raised). STILL OWED: the per-OPERATION half - php failed()/retryFailed()/deadLetters() still FATAL with 'Call to undefined method' on rabbitmq and kafka instead of raising a documented refusal.
